correctness.rationale: The helper implements the inspectable exit/result shell contract: PR-number validation, allow-list load with API_ERROR on missing/empty file, INTERVAL/QUIET_WINDOW/MAX_WAIT defaults, head SHA checks before and after each snapshot with SHA_CHANGED exit 3, paginated REST reviews and GraphQL reviewThreads fetching, on-head review filtering with PENDING blocking terminal, QUIET_ELAPSED when latest actionable age meets QUIET_WINDOW, TIMEOUT at MAX_WAIT, API_ERROR on gh/jq/repo failures, and RESULT=/HEAD= stdout emission with extended fields. Five-point deduction: analyze_snapshot thread_events reads comment .login but GraphQL nodes expose author.login, so unresolved allow-listed bot review threads are never ingested; CONVERGED can therefore fire while actionable bot-authored threads remain, violating the task's dual-condition convergence definition.

quality.rationale: Implementation is clear and repo-consistent: set -euo pipefail, logging.sh sourcing, structured helpers (finish, api_error, run_gh, take_snapshot), canonical bot-allowlist.txt, paginated API access, and focused companion updates to pr-resolve-all.md (preferred helper, result dispatch table, preserved time-based fallback) and AI_REPO_GUIDE.md (tree, table, usage example). Check wiring follows existing patterns (010/105/120/159). Two-point deduction: large inline jq block is not extracted under scripts/lib/jq/ like peer helpers, and the thread field mismatch indicates insufficient alignment between GraphQL shape and snapshot parser.

process.rationale: Diff is tightly scoped to ten on-task files (helper, allow-list, bats, dedicated check, scripts inventory, phase-4 invariant grep, and required prompt/guide/test README updates) with no forbidden live-state surfaces, no PLAN.md or AGENTS.md churn, in-memory-only state, explicit pre-#321 boundary in task constraints, and the documented time-based fallback retained in pr-resolve-all.md.

reliability.rationale: Verification wiring is present and structurally sound: scripts/checks/159-pr-resolve-all-poll.sh invokes run_bats_check; pr-resolve-all-poll.bats stubs gh and asserts all five RESULT branches plus exit codes 0/2/3/4; objective evidence confirms bash -n, lint-shell-conventions, and test_wiring 2/2 pass. Two-point deduction: objective-grade.json skipped bats_poll_helper and full_test_sh so runtime pass is unconfirmed in this bundle, and the bats suite only returns empty reviewThreads nodes—no fixture exercises unresolved bot threads, allow-list edge cases, or pagination—so the primary thread-parsing defect would not be caught.

uncertainty_notes: bats_poll_helper and full_test_sh were skipped in objective-grade.json; subjective reliability assumes stub-based bats cases are structurally sound but not runtime-verified in this bundle.

finish() emits RESULT=<value> HEAD=<sha> plus ELAPSED, LATEST_ACTIONABLE_AGE, PARTICIPATING_BOTS, UNRESOLVED_BOT_THREADS then exits with contract code
take_snapshot fetches head SHA before and after reviews/threads; mismatch triggers finish SHA_CHANGED exit 3
fetch_reviews_json normalizes reviews to {login, state, commitOid} and paginates per_page=100
fetch_threads_json paginates GraphQL reviewThreads via cursor but passes raw nodes with comments.nodes[].author.login
thread_events uses $comments[0].login and select(.login != null) instead of author.login, so thread bots and unresolved counts are never populated
terminal predicate treats empty bot_state_map as true and otherwise requires no PENDING reviews and zero unresolved_threads per participating bot
QUIET_ELAPSED fires when latest_actionable_epoch > 0 and latest_age >= QUIET_WINDOW; TIMEOUT when elapsed_total >= MAX_WAIT
pr-resolve-all.md section 5 documents preferred helper invocation, RESULT dispatch, env defaults, and preserved sleep-based fallback
scripts/tests/pr-resolve-all-poll.bats asserts CONVERGED, QUIET_ELAPSED, SHA_CHANGED, TIMEOUT, and API_ERROR via stub gh but only supplies empty reviewThreads in GraphQL fixtures
